summary: Publishes app provenance, actionable diagnostics and agent authoring documentation. Controller generation semantics are unchanged from 0.0.685.
warning: Existing schema-v1 posts with broad wireSeparation booleans remain readable but cannot authorize an exact separation mechanism. This restriction was introduced before version tracking, in baseline 0.0.685. Publish a new schema-v2 package with evidenced capabilities; do not rewrite installed snapshots.

checklist.schema: Optional manifest.authoredFor added; legacy packages retain their bytes and hashes. Older apps reject packages using the new field.
checklist.events: No execution-event or UPID semantic change from baseline.
checklist.capabilities: No new capability restriction; v2 exact separation requirements are now documented.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No controller-output or audit change; Robofil 2.6.0 retains 2.5.0 source, dialect, output rules and golden fixtures.
checklist.installationAndStorage: Installed packages and saved revisions retain their exact contents. Existing v1/v2 migrations validate ownership and verified originals. Missing manifests with retained files or conflicting backups block opening. New versioned file-transaction journals recover project add/rename/save, complete backup restoration and reviewed cleanup; older apps cannot recover these journals, so finish recovery before downgrading. Settings supports a read-only inventory, verified complete UTF-8 backups up to 128 MiB, empty-destination restore, and explicit stale-checked unreferenced-file cleanup. Journals require temporary storage headroom; quota failure blocks writes. Workbench schema remains 3; no automatic installed-package replacement or cleanup.
checklist.verification: Run release:check, post:docs:check, focused legacy/provenance, package and WebMCP tests, Robofil conformance, package validation, full tests and build before merge. Verify native browser DXF import, machining edits, stale/dirty guards, save, package installation and exact controller output/download, plus package authoring. See PR for results.

publicNotes.summary: Create, check and build complete machine packages in the browser, with downloadable contracts and actionable export diagnostics.
changes: Package workbench checks posts, calculates canonical hashes, hashes evidence files, builds packages and inspects existing archives without a terminal.

Compatible browser agents can import DXF/UPID, inspect geometry, edit machining intent, review execution, save, install machine packages, activate setups and generate/download audited controller files through WebMCP.
New posts can record the app release and versioned documentation they were written for. Older packages retain their exact contents.
Export failures provide a reviewable agent repair prompt with exact versions, diagnostics and browser-based repair steps.

Storage settings can download a complete saved-workbench backup and restore it into an empty destination. Reviewed cleanup requires a saved backup and explicit file selection; installed posts, revisions and migration backups are protected.

Interrupted project saves recover through verified journals. Legacy upgrades preserve originals; missing manifests and conflicting backups produce recovery diagnostics instead of silently replacing data. Finish recovery with the current app before using an older release.
publicNotes.compatibility: Controller output semantics are unchanged from 0.0.685. Existing exact separation and arc-direction requirements still apply. Older app builds can reject the new authoredFor metadata; check a package with the app version you intend to use.
publicNotes.action: Use Package workbench to inspect an existing package. If an update is required, build a new post version, install the complete machine package and activate its setup. An app update does not change installed packages automatically.
